title: Guard that platform-bible-react localization keys actually ship

reviews.author: katherinejensen00
reviews.bodyText:
Thanks for your hard work on this, Jolie!
Here is a summary of all the findings. Giving them to you now so you don't have to wait for me to inline post them.
Findings (numbered, severity-ordered)
1. [Important] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:60

The "every platform-bible-react string key ships somewhere" guard only scans the main package entry, and the platform-bible-react/experimental entry it misses contains a live instance of exactly the bug class this guard exists to catch.
import * as platformBibleReact from 'platform-bible-react' resolves the "." export only. The package also has a "./experimental" entry exporting five more key arrays: RESOURCE_PICKER_DIALOG_STRING_KEYS, SOURCE_LANGUAGE_INDEXED_LIST_STRING_KEYS, NAVIGATION_HISTORY_BUTTONS_STRING_KEYS, INTERNET_ACCESS_OPTION_LIST_STRING_KEYS, DEVELOPER_SECTION_STRING_KEYS. All 8 %sourceLanguageIndexedList_*% keys (source-language-indexed-list.types.ts:68-75) appear in no shipping source — not en/es/fr/km/zh, not any extension contribution, not even the Storybook fixture — while SourceLanguageIndexedList is production-consumed by platform-enhanced-resources via 'platform-bible-react/experimental'. A guard that scanned experimental would fail on all 8 today. Arrays re-exported from neither entry are also invisible (UI_LANGUAGE_SELECTOR_STRING_KEYS, ui-language-selector.component.tsx:13 — its one key does ship, so that one is latent).
To be fair about impact: those 8 keys are currently dead API — the component doesn't even accept a localizedStrings prop yet (plain string props with English defaults), so nothing user-visible changes today, and deleting the dead array would be as valid a resolution as shipping values. But the header comment (lines 52–54, "Every localization key any platform-bible-react component asks for … covered the moment it is exported") and the describe title (line 82) claim coverage the guard doesn't have, with no sign the experimental entry was considered. Suggest either scanning both entries (and explicitly resolving the 8 keys, the same way the BookChapterControl gap was handled mid-review) or scoping the comment/title honestly to the main entry.

2. [Medium] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:1

The guard tests the committed dist bundle, and — contrary to the dismissal recorded in the PR body — no CI step can catch that bundle going stale, so "covered the moment it is exported" (line 52-54) is only true after a manual rebuild-and-commit.
'platform-bible-react' resolves through the workspace symlink to committed dist/index.js (root tsconfig has no path alias for it). Root npm run build runs build:main/extension-host/renderer/types/extensions/data-release — build:platform-bible-react exists but is not in the chain; the lib has no prepare/postinstall hook; link-dev-packages only handles the external yalc repos. So CI's "Verify no files changed after build" step never regenerates this dist and structurally cannot detect staleness (checked exhaustively: chromatic, publish-docs, package-main, e2e — none rebuild it either). The PR body's dismissal of the original stale-dist finding ("test.yml:145 runs npm run build before :166 npm test, so a stale-dist gap fails in CI and cannot reach main") rests on that false premise — the local-latency half of the dismissal was right, but the CI-backstop half isn't.
Mitigating and worth keeping in mind: the app itself consumes the same committed dist, so the guard coherently checks what actually ships, and dist is currently in sync for all 15 arrays. Asks: fix the "covered the moment it is exported" comment, and consider a CI freshness check (rebuild lib + diff) as a follow-up.

3. [Medium] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:78

The "defined in a shipping source" predicate diverges from what a production user can actually resolve, in three ways — the sharpest being that keys "shipping" only via test-gated sample extensions count as shipped.
(a) Any-locale presence passes, but the runtime fallback chain terminates at BACKUP_LANGUAGE = 'en' (localization.service-host.ts:41; unresolved keys warn and return the raw key at 359-362). A key defined only in es.json would pass this guard while English-locale users see raw %key% text. No live instances (the 122 es-only keys are all %Book.*%, which the runtime backfills into en at lines 142-154 — they prove file divergence, not user-visible breakage), but the guard permits the state. (b) getExtensionContributedKeys() reads hello-someone, hello-rock3, and quick-verse, which only load in noisy dev mode (extension.service.ts:100-106, gate at 515-516; resyncContributions receives the post-filter list, so their contributions genuinely never ship). 60 keys "ship" only via those three today; 0 of the 343 guarded keys rely on them, so this is latent — but a key value parked in a sample extension would pass the guard and render raw in production. (c) The union omits fr/km/zh-hans/zh-hant (all six locale files load at runtime) plus the ~124 programmatically-served keys (all %LocalizedId.*%, and %Book.EXO% which es.json alone lacks) — the false-fail direction for a future array referencing them.
A predicate closer to the runtime guarantee would be "defined in an en source among production-loaded contributions" — en is the only guaranteed backstop.

4. [Medium] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:24

SHIPPED_LOCALES = ['en', 'es'] asserts something false by name — six locales ship — and bypasses the getShippedLocaleTags() helper this same PR extracted specifically so tests pick up new locales automatically.
The en/es scope decision for the marker-menu parity block is accepted as litigated (fr/km/zh contain zero markerMenu keys today, and the dismissal reasoning is in the file). The residual findings are narrower: the constant's name misleads (a reader will conclude only two locales ship — assets/localization/ has en, es, fr, km, zh-hans, zh-hant), and the same pair silently feeds the shippingKeys union at line 78, coupling the union's blind spots (finding 3c) to a parity-scoped constant. Renaming (e.g. PARITY_LOCALES with a one-line why-two comment) and deriving the union side from getShippedLocaleTags() would keep the parity choice while removing both problems.

5. [Medium] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:67-69

The discovery pipeline has three silent coverage-loss modes that contradict this file's own fail-loudly design — and the silent-skip branch guards the single array carrying ~62% of the sweep's coverage.
(1) One non-string entry drops an entire array (if (keys.length !== entries.length) return;) with zero signal. The comment defends skip-vs-partially-check but never skip-vs-fail. This matters more than it looks: FOOTNOTE_EDITOR_STRING_KEYS is runtime-composed (...MARKER_MENU_STRING_KEYS, ~186 usfmMarkers description values, ...UNDO_REDO, ...CANCEL_ACCEPT) — one bad entry from a platform-bible-utils regression silently removes ~212 of 343 sweep keys. (2) it.each([]) on vitest 3.2.7 silently creates zero tests (empirically verified — jest throws here, vitest doesn't), so an emptied array loses all coverage unnoticed. (3) The canary only asserts exportedStringKeyArrays.length > 0 (line 85) — erosion from 15 arrays to 1 still passes.
Cheap hardening, all in this file: fail (not skip) on a mixed array; assert each keys.length > 0; assert a minimum array count or snapshot the discovered array names.

6. [Low] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:16-17

The header's stated failure mode — "the real app renders nothing" — is factually wrong: a missing key renders as raw %key% placeholder text, and three independent layers guarantee it.
Traced end-to-end: use-localized-strings-hook.ts:45-49 maps every requested key to itself while loading and on error; localization.service-host.ts:359-362 warns and returns the raw key when nothing resolves; character-marker-control.component.tsx:37-38 does strings[key] ?? key; and at marker-menu.component.tsx:250 that truthy raw string wins the ??. Pre-PR, users saw literal %markerMenu_searchPlaceholder_character% as gray placeholder text — ugly, but not blank. The same claim recurs at line 91 ("renders nothing at all") and in the PR description. In a file that is mostly documentation of a failure mode, the symptom description should match the code; "renders the raw localization key" is the accurate phrasing (and arguably a better motivator, since it's user-visible garbage rather than absence).

7. [Low] — attach at assets/localization/en.json:493-494

Confirming the recorded scope decision on the two %webView_bookChapterControl_*% keys, with two residuals worth capturing before merge: the follow-up ticket, and a casing swap that will happen silently when wiring lands.
Verified independently: BOOK_CHAPTER_CONTROL_STRING_KEYS has zero importers outside the library (nothing preloads these keys, and no call site passes localizedStrings), so "Seleccionar capítulo/versículo" cannot render today — the decision to ship keys now and wire later is recorded in the PR body and not re-litigated here. Residuals: (a) the PR body promises a follow-up ticket for the wiring — please link it before merge so the dead data has an owner; (b) the component's fallbacks are Title Case ('Select Chapter', book-chapter-control.component.tsx:482/484) while these shipped values are sentence case, so whoever wires localization later will silently change visible casing with no test flagging it — worth a note in that ticket; (c) the new guard now reports these keys as "shipping," which dims the very audit signal that would otherwise surface the unwired state.

8. [Low] — attach at extensions/src/platform-scripture-editor/src/localized-strings.test.ts:70-72

"Asserted instead by src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts" transfers less protection than a reader will assume: presence transfers, but the Spanish-differs-from-English assertion its sibling keys get is dropped, not moved.
Every other non-format key in this control's list gets en-presence, es-presence, and es≠en (lines 83-95 of this file). The new guard deliberately declines the differs assertion for all MARKER_MENU keys (its rationale block at shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:38-45), so this key alone permanently loses that protection while sitting in an exclusion list that reads as full delegation. Today's es value is a real translation, so the gap is purely prospective — an untranslated copy-paste would pass everything. Either add a differs check for this key or extend the comment: "presence is asserted there; the differs-from-English check is deliberately not."

9. [Low] — attach at extensions/src/platform-scripture-editor/src/character-marker-control/character-marker-control.const.ts:36-39

The new TSDoc's justification — "Being a platform-shell string rather than an extension-namespaced one" — invents a key category the Localization-Guide doesn't define, and the honest rationale is sibling precedent.
The guide routes strings by "built-in shell UI" vs extension features, and never states that shared-library *_STRING_KEYS values ship in assets/localization/. All consumers of the three markerMenu_searchPlaceholder_* variants live in this one extension, so by the guide's own rule of thumb these would be extension-contribution strings; the actual (good) reason they ship in shell assets is that the whole markerMenu family, _insert/_paragraph included, already lives there. Suggest rewording to cite the precedent ("ships beside its _insert/_paragraph siblings in the shell assets") rather than a category, so future contributors don't cite this comment as license to put single-consumer extension strings into shell assets. Since this PR now also enforces that placement via the guard, recording the "where do shared-library component strings ship" convention in Architecture-Decisions.md (per CLAUDE.md's recording rule) would settle it properly.

10. [Low] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:4-7

This filesystem-dependent test sits under src/shared/ while runtime-importing the @node helper whose own header explains why fs code belongs in src/node/ — the placement contradicts the rule the PR itself cites.
.claude/rules/architecture/shared-patterns.md:26-31: src/shared/ is "Code for ALL processes (including renderer)"; src/node/ is Node-only — no test exemption stated. The helper's header correctly applies that rule to itself; the consuming test performs the same reads via that helper yet lives in src/shared/data/. The in-review discussion recorded in the PR body defended src/** placement (vitest include) and the no-paired-module choice, but not shared-vs-node specifically — and the mid-review helper extraction is what created this residual. Tests are never bundled, so the harm is precedent only; src/node/data/ or src/node/utils/ satisfies the vitest glob equally and keeps the shared tree renderer-safe by inspection.

11. [Low] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:73

This guard and the pre-commit hook now enforce overlapping "shipping sources" definitions that neither references, and they already disagree.
.husky/lib/ai-hooks.sh run_localization_check validates staged %key% usage against assets/localization/en.json (line 299) and extensions/src/*/contributions/localizedStrings.json (line 303), while excluding lib/ files (line 278) — so key introductions inside the library are structurally invisible to it, and it accepts en-only while this guard accepts en∪es∪extensions. When a shipping source changes (new locale, moved contributions), two unlinked enforcement points need coordinated edits. A cross-reference comment in each would prevent drift; the deeper follow-up question is whether the hook's lib/ exclusion should be removed — noting the hook is husky-local and never runs in CI, so this test is currently the only merge-blocking enforcement.

12. [Low] — attach at src/node/utils/locale-assets.test-helper.ts:56-61

getExtensionContributedKeys hardcodes contributions/localizedStrings.json, but the real loader is manifest-driven — the helper's corpus and the shipping corpus can silently diverge.
contribution.service.ts:122-129 reads the path from each manifest's localizedStrings field. Today all 10 declaring manifests use exactly the conventional path (evil and c-sharp-provider-test declare none), so the helper matches reality — but a manifest pointing elsewhere makes the guard miss real shipping keys (false failures), and an orphaned conventional-path file not referenced by any manifest would count keys the app never loads (false passes). Reading each manifest's localizedStrings field instead is a small change that also gives you the extension names, which is what you'd need to exclude the noisy-dev-gated test extensions (finding 3b).

13. [Low] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:73-76

The shipping model here omits the metadata fallbackKey mechanism, so a key legitimately served entirely through a fallback chain would fail this guard despite localizing correctly.
The runtime resolves one level of metadata fallbackKey (from assets/localization/metadata.json and contribution metadata blocks — localization.service-host.ts:245-278) before falling back to en and then the raw key; the %cancelButton_tooltip% → %general_cancel% entry is the established pattern. Verified that zero shipped keys are fallbackKey-only today, so this is purely latent — but a future dedup migration onto fallbackKey would false-fail here and pressure someone into re-adding duplicate values. A sentence in the "Two sources ship" comment acknowledging the exclusion (or folding metadata keys into the union) closes it.

14. [Low] — attach at src/node/utils/locale-assets.test-helper.ts:63-66

The helper re-declares contribution and locale-map shapes that platform-bible-utils already exports as the canonical contract, becoming the third hand-rolled parser of these files in the test suite.
LocalizedStringDataContribution (lib/platform-bible-utils/src/extension-contributions/localized-strings.model.ts:21) and LanguageStrings (:83) are exported from the package entry and already imported by five src/node files, so the import is free. The inline { localizedStrings?: Record<string, Record<string, string>> } here (and the Record<string, string> at lines 33-36) duplicates that contract beside two sibling hand-rolled readers (platform-scripture-editor and legacy-comment-manager localized-strings tests) with nothing linking the three — a format change now requires coordinated edits nothing points to. Use the canonical types, and consider a cross-reference comment naming the sibling readers.

15. [Low] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:59

A batch of small simplifications in this file; the notable one is that the comment justifying the imperative discovery loop overstates the constraint — a type-safe declarative form does compile.
(a) Object.entries<unknown>(...).flatMap(([arrayName, exported]) => ... && exported.every((k): k is string => typeof k === 'string') ? [{arrayName, keys: exported}] : []) typechecks clean on the repo's TS (verified by compilation) — the comment's impossibility claim only applies to the filter-plus-tuple-predicate variant it replaced. (b) The [...MARKER_MENU_STRING_KEYS]/[...keys] spreads at lines 46/95 are unnecessary — line 37 already passes the readonly SHIPPED_LOCALES tuple to describe.each directly, and it.each([...] as const) precedent exists in reference-history-keyboard.util.test.ts. (c) Lines 1-2 import the same module twice (namespace + named); platformBibleReact.MARKER_MENU_STRING_KEYS would drop one. (d) The 7 marker-menu keys are triple-asserted — their sweep entries can never fail independently, since shippingKeys ⊇ en keys asserted at line 47. (e) The "(12 en-only keys, 122 es-only)" counts appear at both line 20 and line 93 — accurate today (verified), which is exactly how they'll rot silently and independently.

16. [Low] — attach at src/node/utils/locale-assets.test-helper.ts:33-36

Small robustness/clarity batch in the helper: unattributed parse failures, a redundant intermediate variable with a duplicated justification comment, and a header that under-describes the module.
(a) All JSON.parse calls here run at consuming-test module load with no try/catch and no path context — one malformed contribution file fails the whole guard file at collection with a bare SyntaxError naming no file; wrapping with the offending path turns that into a findable failure. (b) readShippedLocale's intermediate strings variable exists only to carry an annotation the declared return type already provides, and its "JSON.parse returns any…" comment is near-duplicated at line 64 (the same comment family now has six repo instances — worth stating once per module at most). (c) The header says "helpers for reading the real shipped locale assets in assets/localization/", but a third of the module reads extensions/src contributions — a developer hunting for contribution-reading helpers will skip this file on its header.

17. [Low, constructive] — attach at lib/platform-bible-react/src/localizedStrings.json:210

The five-copies maintenance surface this PR just exercised (en.json, es.json, fixture en, fixture es, story arg) remains unguarded — and a fixture⊆shipping subset check would land green today and would have caught the original incident directly.
Verified: all 211 fixture keys are currently in the shipping union (zero exceptions), and the original bug was precisely "in fixture, absent from shipping." A one-test addition to the new guard file — every key in this fixture must exist in a shipping source — inverts the root cause structurally, and covers recurrence classes the array-driven sweep can't see: keys requested via string literals, dynamic keys like %scrollGroup_*%, and any future component whose array isn't exported per the naming convention. The complementary mechanism-level option: the runtime already logger.warns on every unresolved key (localization.service-host.ts:359-361); nothing surfaces that in CI or e2e today.

18. [Info] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:46-47

toBeTruthy() makes the parity test's title slightly dishonest at the edges: a defined-but-empty value fails under "defines %s", while a whitespace or stray-* value passes as defined.
Pure polish, no live instance. If the intent is "defines a usable string," expect(...).toBeTypeOf('string') plus a non-empty-after-trim check states it exactly; if the intent really is presence, the title could say "defines a non-empty value for %s".

19. [Info] — attach at extensions/src/platform-scripture-editor/src/character-marker-control/character-marker-control.component.test.tsx:271

Optional consistency choice: the reworded placeholder literal now appears three times in this file (STRINGS map line 48, queries at 271 and 353) — referencing the map would make future rewords one-line, at the cost of assertion independence.
Both styles are defensible and the repo uses both: repeating the literal keeps the assertion independent of the fixture that feeds the component (a corrupted STRINGS value can't self-verify), while getByPlaceholderText(STRINGS['%markerMenu_searchPlaceholder_character%']) eliminates the update-one-miss-two hazard this PR just navigated. Flagging as a choice, not a defect.

20. [Info] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:95-96

Scale observation: the per-key it.each yields 359 tests for three logical invariants, with substantial duplicate coverage inside the sweep, and the count grows by one for every key ever added to any library component.
Counts verified (343 sweep + 14 parity + 2 canaries — the PR body's 359 is exact). Within the sweep, SELECT_BOOKS_STRING_KEYS and SCOPE_SELECTOR_STRING_KEYS are identical 17-key sets, and FOOTNOTE_EDITOR_STRING_KEYS re-spreads MARKER_MENU/UNDO_REDO/CANCEL_ACCEPT — so ~100+ sweep tests re-assert keys already asserted under another describe. An aggregated per-array assertion (expect(keys.filter(k => !shippingKeys.has(k))).toEqual([])) gives the same failure diagnostics in ~16 tests. Per-key granularity has repo precedent in the extension's own localized-strings test, so this is taste — noting it mainly for the growth rate.

21. [Info] — attach at src/shared/data/shipped-locale-assets.test.ts:74-75

One-line comment fix: "(which is where the %webView_*% keys legitimately live)" is contradicted two files away in this same PR, which ships two %webView_*% keys in the shell assets.
%webView_bookChapterControl_selectChapter/selectVerse% land in assets/localization/en.json:493-494 (and en.json already carried %webView_defaultTitle_webView%, %webView_edit%, %webView_error_dump_*%). Together with the "platform-shell string" TSDoc (finding 9), the PR's two new placement comments describe incompatible taxonomies. Suggested wording: "where extension-owned %webView_*% keys live."

22. [Info — out of scope, file separately rather than as a PR comment]

While auditing the locale corpus we found a pre-existing gap unrelated to this PR: es.json defines %Book.*% for 122 of 123 canon book IDs — %Book.EXO% is missing (and es has no %LocalizedId.*% entries at all), so Spanish users see English "Exodus" via the en runtime backfill while every other book shows Spanish. Cheap to fix; worth a ticket rather than a comment on this PR.

Re-review — round 2 at 433684e
Re-reviewed after the merge from main. CI is green (ubuntu-22.04 and windows-latest Build passed), and I confirmed the new guard passes locally: 359 tests in shipped-locale-assets.test.ts, 11 in language-details.data.test.ts, and 140 across the eight touched extension test files. Nothing here is a test failure. The findings below are about what the guard does and doesn't actually protect.
Corrections to my round-1 findings
Two things I asserted in round 1 were wrong, and both cut in your favour on one point and against on another.
Finding 13 was wrong. I said "zero shipped keys are fallbackKey-only today." Three exist right now, each with a fallbackKey in assets/localization/metadata.json and no value in either en.json or es.json: %resources_type_ER% to %ProjectType_17%, %submit% to %yes%, and %yes% to %confirm%. There are 28 fallbackKey entries and 17 deprecationInfo entries in total. So the false-failure I described as purely latent is a live pattern.
Finding 5(2) was wrong. I said it.each([]) silently registers zero tests on vitest 3.2.7. It does not. I probed it directly and vitest raises Error: No test found in suite . An emptied array fails loudly, so that part of finding 5 can be dropped. Findings 5(1) and 5(3) still stand, and the genuinely silent path is the keys.length !== entries.length early return at line 69, which prevents the describe from registering at all.

The false-failure ofrom a currentlyguarded key.
%scripture_section_dc_long% is a member of BOOK_CHAPTER_CONTROL_STRING_KEYS and already carries a fallbackKey in metadata.json. Retire its value the way the Localization Guide documents — delete the value, keep the fallbackKey — and this guard goes red on a key that renders correctly at runtime. The pressure on whoever hits that wbe to re-add obsolete n.


The merge reintroduced the exact divergence this PR closes, in two places.


At r1 (5609e86) the branch was clean and grep -rn "Search character markers" returned nothing. The merge from main brought two sites back:

lib/platform-bible-react/src/components/advanced/marker-menu.stories.tsx:313, a new story still using the old wording while its sibling at line 275 has the new value.
extensions/src/platform-scripture-editor/src/character-marker-bar/character-marker-bar.component.test.tsx:72, a new component's STRINGS fixture carrying both the old value and a copy of the old-style "Lives in platform-bible-react" comment this PR rewrites elsewhere.

Both are self-consistent fixtures, so no test fails and CI stays green. Two one-line edits, but the point is that the guard checks key presence  and never value agreemt catch this class.

The PR premise is now obsolete and the body needs rewriting before    squash.

%markerMenu_searchPlaceholder_character% reached main independently via #2660 (22f2886) with the identical value. Commit caeb003 therefore contributes zero lines to the diff against main, and gh pr diff shows en.json adding only the two %webView_bookChapterControl_*% keys.

B2 — [Scope] The new ADR records as Accepted a rule that 82 live keys violate, and names an enforcer that does not enforce it
.context/standards/Architecture-Decisions.md:1292 (and the same text at
.context/standards/Localization-Guide.md:190)
The ADR's Decision says a platform-bible-react component's values ship in the shell's assets
"never in one extension's contributions/localizedStrings.json, regardless of how many
extensions consume the component today" — then says shipped-locale-assets.test.ts "enforces it."
Neither half holds. Enumerating every key in every *_STRING_KEYS array literal under
lib/platform-bible-react/src and cross-checking against en.json plus every production-loaded
extension contribution:
total library declared keys: 147
in en.json:                   65
extension-contribution-only:  82

Spot-verified: %webView_book_selector_books_selected%, _select_books%, _more% — all absent
from en.json, all present in extensions/src/platform-scripture/contributions/localizedStrings.json.
Two whole arrays live that way (INVENTORY_STRING_KEYS, SELECT_BOOKS_STRING_KEYS), plus two
DEVELOPER_SECTION_STRING_KEYS members in paratext-registration.
That is precisely the shape the ADR lists and rejects as Alternative (a). And the guard accepts it
by design — shippingKeys at :120-124 unions getExtensionContributedKeys('en') as a first-class
English shipping source, so it will never flag one of those 82.
This matters more than a wording nit because CLAUDE.md treats the decision log as a durable standard
that agents read and enforce on the next feature. An entry stating a "never" that 56% of live
library keys violate will generate false findings against existing code, and a developer following
Localization-Guide step 4 literally would start migrating INVENTORY_STRING_KEYS out of
platform-scripture — a large migration this PR neither performs nor scopes.
Two smaller overstatements ride along in the same paragraph: the guard does not cover "every key in
every exported *_STRING_KEYS array" (the test's own comment at :92 concedes
UI_LANGUAGE_SELECTOR_STRING_KEYS is exported from neither entry and stays invisible), and
Consequences' "CI fails when it is skipped" is qualified two lines later by the dist/ staleness
caveat.
Decision needed: narrow the Decision to what the guard actually enforces ("must be defined in
some English shipping source; the shell assets are the default home for a shared-library string"),
or commit to the strict rule with an explicit grandfather clause plus a migration ticket.
